questions.q: Who are the two sponsors of the company-wide platform review that opens this capstone?
options: Priya Suresh and Theo Bryant
Casey Lindqvist, VP of Engineering, and Dana Whitfield, the new CTO
Two outside consultants hired for the sale
The Driftwood board of directors, acting as a committee
questions.explain: Casey Lindqvist (VP of Engineering) and Dana Whitfield (the newly hired CTO) co-sponsor the review and are the named stakeholders Theo now answers to.

questions.q: What are the platform review's three findings?
options: The budget is too small, the team is too small, and the deadline is too short
No shared platform across teams, no credible cost/capacity forecast for 10x traffic, and no shared visibility when something goes wrong
Too many clouds, too many vendors, and too much documentation
The product-catalog app is outdated and needs a full rewrite
questions.explain: The review found every team's infrastructure is a one-off, nobody could forecast cost or capacity at scale, and there was no single shared view of platform health or spend.

questions.q: What is the actual mandate that comes out of the review?
options: Rewrite the product-catalog app in a new language
Migrate containerized services onto Kubernetes at real scale across both clouds, with a shared FinOps dashboard, proven under real load during the company's biggest sale
Switch entirely from Azure to AWS to simplify billing
Hire a dedicated SRE team before touching any infrastructure
questions.explain: The mandate is a real-scale, multi-cloud Kubernetes migration with a shared FinOps dashboard, tested for real during Driftwood's biggest sale of the year.

questions.q: What is Dana Whitfield's core pushback on using the intermediate project as proof the bigger platform will work?
options: The intermediate project used the wrong programming language
One app surviving one deploy on one node is a different claim than a dozen services, scaled under real holiday traffic, staying inside budget — and the second claim needs its own proof
The intermediate project was never actually deployed to production
Dana doesn't trust Theo's technical skills
questions.explain: Dana's point is that a working pilot and a platform proven at scale under real load are different claims, and the review requires the second claim to be demonstrated, not assumed.

questions.q: What has NOT yet been decided as of the end of this lesson?
options: Theo's job title
Which services move to Kubernetes first, which cloud is primary vs. backup, and what the FinOps dashboard actually measures
The name of the company
Whether Driftwood will run a holiday sale this year
questions.explain: This lesson covers why the mandate exists, not the plan — scope, cloud architecture, and dashboard design are explicitly left to the next two lessons.
